sources.note: Awarding body's own page: Ministry for Pacific Peoples (mpp.govt.nz, New Zealand Government), programme page for Toloa Scholarships.
Le Va, the body that administers the Toloa Scholarships on behalf of the Ministry for Pacific Peoples; carries full eligibility criteria, dates and funding detail.

awarding_body.detail: The page is the Ministry for Pacific Peoples' own site (New Zealand government domain). It confirms the Ministry funds the scholarships, administered by Le Va.
awarding_body.quote: The Ministry for Pacific Peoples funds the Toloa scholarships, which are administered by Le Va. Le Va manages the application process, disbursement of funds, and reporting.

deadline.detail: The published tertiary deadline is 5pm, Monday 9 February 2026, exactly as the record states. Both pages state applications are now closed: 'Applications for 2026 tertiary scholarships are now closed' and 'Applications for the 2026 Toloa Scholarships are now closed.' No 2027 round dates are published as of 12 October 2026, so there is no currently-open cycle to verify against.
deadline.quote: Tertiary scholarship applications closed at 5pm on Monday 9 February 2026.

eligibility.detail: Every distinct record claim is confirmed: Pacific descent students who have completed at least one year, continuing full-time STEM study in New Zealand, entering second year or beyond. Le Va adds detail the record omits: applicants must be New Zealand citizens or permanent residents of Pacific Islands descent, enrolment must be at a New Zealand tertiary institution, and final-year students covered by the Government fees-free programme are excluded.
eligibility.quote: Scholarships for tertiary students in 2026 are available to those who have completed at least one year of study and are continuing full-time STEM study. Students entering their second year or beyond may apply.

funding.detail: The award is partial, not fully funded: up to $10,000 for one year of full-time study, paid directly to the tertiary institution. It is broader than the record's 'Tuition Fee Waiver' label - it may cover tuition, compulsory course-related costs, university hall accommodation and (for PhD students) research or fieldwork expenses. The record correctly does not claim Fully Funded.
funding.quote: Tertiary students in STEM courses can receive up to $10,000 for one year of full-time study. This may cover tuition, compulsory course related costs, accommodation expenses for university halls and, for PhD students, research or fieldwork expenses.

degree_levels.detail: Tertiary level only for this record: second year or beyond of a full-time STEM programme at a New Zealand tertiary institution. First-year students are excluded.
degree_levels.quote: be enrolled full-time in your second year of study in a STEM-related programme at a New Zealand tertiary institution in 2026, and provide proof of enrolment

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: 5 pm, Monday 9 February 2026 (tertiary applications closed; no 2027 round dates published as at 12 October 2026)
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: All record claims check out against the Ministry's own page and Le Va's administration page; only 10 tertiary awards are offered per year. The 2026 round closed 9 February 2026 (applications had opened 10am Tuesday 18 November 2025); as of 12 October 2026 no 2027 cycle dates are published, so the record cannot be marked active. Next re-check should occur around November 2026 for the 2027 round on the MPP education page and the Le Va Toloa page. Also note: eligibility includes New Zealand citizenship or permanent residency plus Pacific descent, students eligible for the government final-year fees-free scheme are excluded, and the award is up to $10,000 paid to the institution covering tuition and other approved study costs - the funding_type label 'Tuition Fee Waiver' understates the coverage.

notes_for_reviewer: Record is factually accurate for the closed 2026 cycle but not currently actionable - do not mark active until the 2027 round opens. A human should also decide whether funding_type 'Tuition Fee Waiver' should be relabelled (the actual award is 'up to $10,000 for one year of full-time study' covering tuition and other approved costs) and whether the eligibility_summary should add the citizenship/permanent-residency and Pacific-descent requirement and the fees-free exclusion.
